core.title: Open every implementation file with its component URN marker
core.given: An implementation file — production source or markup artifact, of a file kind the profile scans — whose name matches none of the profile's test-exempt patterns and that lies in no tree on the profile's never-scanned vendored/generated list
core.when: the file exists in scope (new, edited or pre-existing)
core.then: Its first meaningful line MUST be its component URN marker, written in the binding syntax the profile prescribes for the file's kind, preceded only by blank lines and an allowed preamble (an interpreter directive or a document-type declaration).
prefer: During GREEN: derive the URN from the plan ownership of the implementation being added.
During GREEN: write the marker in the binding syntax the profile prescribes for the file's kind (source-comment syntax in code, markup-comment syntax in templates).
During GREEN: add only the marker; don't restructure a correctly placed file.
avoid: Marker below the imports or any other content (reads as missing).
Inventing a plan ownership unit — a feature, component, side, or layer — that the plan does not define.
Copying a nearby file's URN without verifying ownership.
Moving code merely to make the marker easier to write.
unless: Test files — defined exactly as files whose name matches one of the profile's test-exempt patterns: bound by their acceptance URNs instead.
Vendored and generated trees (the profile's single never-scanned list): never scanned.
An interpreter directive (shebang) or a document-type declaration may precede the marker.
core.why: The component URN is the only edge between an implementation file and the plan graph; without it no acceptance can claim the file, no plan slice owns it, and coverage cannot see it exists.
evidence: The stack's traceability check reports no marker finding for in-scope implementation files.
The file is traceable from its real component URN (the URN matches the plan ownership of the implementation).
verification: A repository-wide check scans every in-scope implementation file of the profile's source and markup file kinds — whether new, edited or pre-existing, not gated on operation, phase or a prior finding — and reports a finding for each whose first meaningful line is not its component URN marker in the profile's binding syntax.

Scan-scope exclusions, owned by the checker and defined by pattern and path membership, not by role assignment: a file whose name matches one of the profile's test-exempt patterns is not scanned — it binds acceptance URNs instead — and a file merely assigned a test role whose name matches no such pattern stays in scope; likewise no tree on the profile's single never-scanned vendored/generated list is scanned.

Header-region tolerance (detector tolerance, not coder permission): the leading run of blank lines, an optional interpreter directive or document-type declaration, and single-line comments form the header region; the first real content line ends it, so a marker below the imports or other content reads as missing.
First meaningful line: the first line that is neither blank nor a preamble; an interpreter directive or document-type declaration is not content and must not displace the marker.

The traceability header — the leading comment block binding a file to the plan graph, whose fields and comment syntaxes the profile defines — is not checked as a whole: this rule covers only the component URN marker within it.
Disposition strict: the check fails on every finding; severity 3; no advisory mode, no ratchet baseline.

fires: Creating or editing an in-scope implementation source file whose first meaningful line is not its component URN marker
Creating or editing an in-scope markup artifact whose first meaningful line is not its component URN marker
An existing, untouched in-scope implementation file — of a scanned file kind, matching no test-exempt pattern, in no never-scanned tree — that lacks the marker
An implementation file whose URN marker sits below the imports or other content
doesNotFire: A file whose name matches one of the profile's test-exempt patterns (they bind acceptance URNs instead); pattern match alone exempts, never test-role assignment, so a test-role file without a matching pattern still fires
Files in the trees on the profile's single never-scanned vendored/generated list
A file whose first meaningful line is the URN marker, preceded only by blank lines and an allowed interpreter directive or document-type declaration

profileRequirements.meaning: Suffixes or name patterns of the production implementation source files this rule scans.
Suffixes or name patterns of the markup artifacts (templates) this rule scans.

Name patterns whose match exempts a file from this marker obligation (it binds acceptance URNs instead); the exemption is exactly pattern membership — a test-role file whose name matches none of these patterns stays in scope.
The stack's single never-scanned list of vendored and generated trees.
The syntax by which an implementation file opens with its component URN marker, per file kind (source vs markup).
profileRequirements.bunValue: // URN: component:… in source; <!-- URN: component:… --> in markup templates

profileRequirements.meaning: The concrete fields of the traceability header — the leading comment block binding a file to the plan graph — and its per-kind comment syntax; this rule checks only the component URN marker within it, not the other fields.
profileRequirements.bunValue: URN, Tested-By, Runtime, Purpose; `//` in source, `<!-- … -->` in .html templates

bunOnly.text: bun_green_traceability_detector reports no GREEN-URN-001 / BUN-GREEN-URN-MARKER-001 finding for in-scope implementation files.
bunOnly.reason: Detector, validator and finding ids are realization details; the core states the same check generically.

bunOnly.text: Unlike the Vite sibling (which counts a shebang as the first non-empty line and so reports a header it actually has as missing), this realization skips the shebang.
bunOnly.reason: A comparison between sibling stack realizations' detectors; it carries no stack-neutral obligation and adds nothing the core could impose.

neutralityNotes: Nothing unneutralizable at the obligation level: the scanned file kinds, the binding syntax, the traceability-header field list and both exclusion lists live in the profile (suffix.source, suffix.markup, suffix.test_exempt, urn.binding.component, urn.header#traceability_header, roots.excluded — all existing vocabulary keys, no proposals), so the core names no stack, suffix or path. Revision-3 fixes from feedback: (1) the test-file exclusion is now defined everywhere — facts, fires, doesNotFire, unless and verification — exactly by suffix.test_exempt pattern membership, never by test-role assignment, so a test-role file without a matching pattern remains in scope, matching Bun's filename-pattern exclusion; (2) the concrete traceability-header field list moved from bunOnly into profile data as urn.header#traceability_header, while the core keeps the neutral header definition and the marker-only scope without expanding the check. Remaining judgment calls: 'product capability' was generalized to 'plan ownership unit / plan slice'; the Vite-sibling detector comparison (verifier_detail[4]) has no neutral equivalent and stays bunOnly, as do detector/validator/finding ids (evidence[0]) per the notProfileKeys rule.
